core's parseYaml reads a plain scalar continued on the next line inside a flow sequence (`[1⏎2]` is `['1 2']`), as the YAML 1.2 spec allows; js-yaml 4, which v12 used, rejects it (`missed comma between flow collection entries`). core's parseYaml rejects a tab-indented plain scalar document (`tabs are not allowed for indentation`), where js-yaml 4, which v12 used, read it as text; v12 then ignored the non-mapping data. Only the generated tabs variant writes it (core YAML, not kanban; #453).

A colour difference, not a parse one: under `theme: dark` with `themeVariables.darkMode: true` v13 lightens the columns (`lightenHsl(cScale<n>, 10%)`), as `theme: dark` alone does in both, where v12's adjuster darkened them on the author's darkMode (D741, amends D374). Source: `---
config:
  theme: dark
  themeVariables:
    darkMode: true
---
kanban
  todo[Todo]
    a[Card]
`. No corpus item has this id, so the parity runner never observes it; `packages/conformance/src/kanban/theme.spec.ts` checks it against v12's style sheet (MIGRATION 220-kanban).

A layout difference, not a parse one: a word wider than its wrap (a column title, card title, ticket or assignee) is split between characters, so no text crosses its column's or card's right edge, where v12 kept it whole and let it overflow (D765, amends D372). Source: `e2e/diagrams/kanban/nightly-check/long-words.mmd`, whose hash this is; its models agree, so the parity runner never observes this entry. `packages/diagram-kanban/src/layout/layout.spec.ts` and the layout invariants (`kanbanLayoutViolations`, swept by `packages/conformance/src/kanban/layout-corpus.spec.ts`) check it (MIGRATION 220-kanban, #1304).

A layout difference, not a parse one: card text (title, ticket, assignee) wraps at `W − cardInset − 2·labelInset` (165 px at the default width), where v12 measured it at `W − 25`, so every line ends `labelInset` inside the card's right edge; column titles wrap at `W − 2·labelInset`, where v12 wrapped them at `W`; and the least `kanban.sectionWidth` is 36 px, where v13 had 26 (D764, amends D372).
